problem: Topological maps built via random-walk exploration (SPTM) are inefficient, while active exploration methods (active SLAM, RL) need metric inputs (depth, pose, occupancy) and millions of training images.
motivation: A metric-free, lightweight exploration policy that generalizes to unseen environments would make topological mapping simple and cheap in hardware and data. Observation: exploration can be framed as task and motion planning done entirely in image feature space and learned by imitating easy-to-get expert coverage demonstrations.
key_idea: An LSTM task planner hallucinates the next-best image feature and an MLP motion planner maps (current, hallucinated) features to an action, jointly trained by deeply-supervised imitation of expert exploration demonstrations, with VLAD-based VPR closing loops in the resulting topological map.
insight: Deep supervision at every step of both planners is essential: removing both (NoDeepSup) drops MP3D coverage to 0.292, below RandomWalk (0.301), versus 0.642 for the full model. Feature-space hallucination generalizes better than action-space planning (NoFeatHallu 0.589 vs 0.642 on MP3D; LSTMActRegu 0.610), and the naive history memory hurts generalization (0.618), suggesting short-term memory suffices here.
method: Feature extractor: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet18 encodes 256x512 panoramic RGB into a 512-d feature, jointly fine-tuned with the planners.
TaskPlanner: two-layer LSTM over the latest m=10 features hallucinates the next best feature f_{t+1}, trained with L2 loss on every step's hallucination.
MotionPlanner: MLP over concat(f_t, hallucinated f_{t+1}) classifies one of 3 actions (forward, left, right) with cross-entropy, also supervised at every step.

Expert demonstrations: sample anchor points over the navigable area and repeatedly walk to the nearest unvisited anchor with Habitat PathFollower, recording panoramic RGB and actions (about 0.45M images).
Topological mapping: append each observation and action as node and edge; VLAD descriptors from SIFT (k=16) in a ball tree find visually similar node pairs (threshold 1.15) as loop-closure edges.
ActionAssigner: ResNet18 with a BiLSTM predicts a 6-step action list for each VPR-added edge.
Navigation: localize start and goal images on the map via VPR and run Dijkstra to get the action path; a simple obstacle-avoidance rule is applied during exploration.

setting.backbone: ResNet18 + 2-layer LSTM + MLP (trained end-to-end by imitation, ResNet18 ImageNet-initialized)
setting.training_data: Expert exploration demonstrations on Gibson train (72 scenes), about 0.45M panoramic RGB images with actions, generated by an oracle anchor-point traversal
setting.observation: panoramic RGB 256x512 only (plus a distance sensor/LiDAR for obstacle avoidance)
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: move_forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 10° (also 0.30 m / 30° variant)
setting.privileged: none at test time (expert oracle demonstrations used only for training; obstacle-distance sensing used during exploration)

numbers.eval_set_note: 14 Gibson val scenes, 71 random starts per scene

numbers_note: Exploration benchmarks are non-canonical coverage tasks; the MP3D navigation entry uses 'MP3D-ImageNav' (not in the canonical list) and could map to HM3D-ImageNav/Gibson-ImageNav-style benchmarks.
results: On MP3D zero-shot exploration DeepExplorer reaches 64.2% coverage (109 m²), beating ANS (52.1%, 73.3 m²), and on Gibson it is comparable to ANS (91.8% vs 94.8%) with a larger covered area (35.3 vs 32.7 m²). For image-goal navigation it beats ANS (SR 95.7 vs 95.1 on Gibson; 73.3 vs 59.3 on MP3D) using RGB only, 0.45M training images and a 16M model.
limitations: Short-term memory only; inefficient, locally repetitive exploration in complex, narrow layouts, and the simple history variant did not help.
Sim2real failures: glass walls are mistaken for open doorways, and real-world evidence is only qualitative with no quantitative metrics.
Needs an obstacle-avoidance heuristic and expert demonstrations (oracle in sim), and real-world tests used LiDAR for obstacle avoidance.
